title: A duality of misère games and play with a pass
summary: In combinatorial game theory, the choice of play convention is a fundamental aspect of the theory. The two most widely studied conventions are normal play, in which the player who makes the last move wins, and misère play, in which the player who makes the last move loses. Another well-known variant is play with a single shared pass. In such games, at most one pass may be used in total during the game: once the pass has been used, neither player may pass thereafter.
